answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost. A knoll stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a pearl holds the rep...
